title: Time Athena's request-to-merge steps, fix top delays, show speedup
summary: Goal: carry out RM-0 item 4 and 3a of the roadmap (BRIEF.md:494-496). Athena's owner and maintainers need to see where time goes between request and merge, including CI and waits. Measure each step, fix the largest delays (likely CI setup and caching in .github/workflows/ci.yml), and show before and after wall times.

defaults_applied.how: Success is judged by measured wall time per verified result before and after, not by the timing code existing.
Timings cite their records or CI runs; unmeasured numbers are labeled estimates.
New timing code has tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
One focused change: measure, then fix the largest delay.
The fix targets the measured biggest delay rather than a guess.
Criteria check the report output and the before/after speedup, not just that files exist.
An empty set of timing records is reported as no data, not as success.
A check guards against the check count falling while wall time improves.
Timing code is written in Rust.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: the user and maintainers judging whether Athena got faster.
The existing per-invocation wall_time records, CI run durations and docs/design/ci-routing.md section 9 are the data sources; no new external service is added.

Scope is one focused change: a timing report per step (job phases plus CI and wait time) and the single largest fix, most likely CI caching keyed on Cargo.lock and the toolchain, or avoiding duplicate check runs.
The earlier sccache attempt (D80) was removed in D84 because its cause could not be reproduced, so any cache fix must measure hits first.
Measured numbers come from real records or CI runs; any number not measured is labeled an estimate.
The reading rests on a code change in Rust; CI workflow edits are included only if the measured biggest delay is in CI.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status` (or the new timing subcommand) and see wall time per step from request to merged, with CI and waiting time reported as separate rows.
A baseline-versus-after table lists measured wall times per step, cites the records or CI runs it came from, and labels any estimate as an estimate.
The top delays are ranked by measured time, and the change fixes at least the largest one. The fix is traceable to a recorded timing (AD-11).
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, and the new timing code has tests covering step durations, missing timestamps and an empty record set, which must not read as success.
If .github/workflows/ci.yml changes, it is named in the change, actions stay pinned by SHA, permissions stay read-only, and no check is removed (check count does not fall).
CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md and docs/design/roadmap.md record the decision and the measured outcome; no secrets or personal data are committed.

out_of_scope: Building the full concurrent-jobs feature from parallel-jobs.md
Re-adding sccache without measured hit counts
Weakening or removing any verification check to gain speed
departures: The request is broad (measure, fix, and prove speedup, with CI involved) and the 'show it got faster' part needs real CI timings that may not be available inside a job. Cost, time and pass odds are therefore worse than the reference.
